# Why Baꜥal is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Baꜥal** is what the evidence put back.

The Ugaritic Baꜥal Cycle (KTU 1.1–1.6) is the central myth of Canaanite religion. It tells how Baꜥal wins kingship from the chaotic Sea, builds his palace, confronts Death, and returns to bring back the rains. The cycle is a seasonal drama of drought and renewal, but also a political statement about divine legitimacy. Ēl grants kingship to Yamm, the Sea, who sends messengers demanding that Baꜥal be delivered as a slave.  Baꜥal refuses.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Baꜥal
- **ASCII form:** baal
- **Meaning:** "Canaanite storm and fertility god; the title "Lord" (baʿlu) was also applied to local deities"
- **Domain of influence:** Storm God, Lord of the Heavens
- **Pantheon:** Canaanite
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𐎁𐎓𐎍
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 48 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Βαάλ**. On the evidence, it means "Canaanite storm and fertility god; the title "Lord" (baʿlu) was also applied to local deities".

**Baꜥal** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *baal* and **Baꜥal** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Baꜥal** lives at [/sites/baal/](/sites/baal/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/baal/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/baal/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/baal/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Baꜥal** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** — The storm whose return ends the drought; the Levantine harvest rides on his rain.
- **Meteorology & Weather Intelligence** — The storm made king, who rides the clouds and opens his palace windows for the rain — the Levant’s weather enthroned.
- **Disaster Resilience & Recovery** — Swallowed by Death and back with the rains; the drought-and-renewal cycle is the oldest recovery narrative.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Canaanite tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Enūma Eliš](/texts/enuma-elish/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
